title: termctl open --json
description: The pane object plus focused and decision_ids. pid is null when no process was recorded. With state gone, pane_id, window_id, display_name and session are the last known values.

name.description: Read from a pane option: untrusted, since anything with access to the socket can write it; a hook gate that must hold must not rely on it.

marker.description: Read from a pane option: untrusted, since anything with access to the socket can write it; a hook gate that must hold must not rely on it.

marker_text.description: The stored text (@termctl_marker_text). Read from a pane option: untrusted, since anything with access to the socket can write it; a hook gate that must hold must not rely on it.

labels.description: Read from a pane option: untrusted, since anything with access to the socket can write it; a hook gate that must hold must not rely on it.

placement.description: Read from a pane option: untrusted, since anything with access to the socket can write it; a hook gate that must hold must not rely on it.

session.description: For a linked window, the first session tmux lists for it.

pid.description: The recorded PID, used only for signaling; null if none was recorded. Read from a pane option: untrusted, since anything with access to the socket can write it; a hook gate that must hold must not rely on it.

state.description: gone: the pane had already closed when open returned, or its state could not be read.

exit_status.description: Set when dead and the command exited normally. Both exit fields may be null for a dead pane.

exit_signal.description: Set when dead by a signal; null on tmux older than 3.3.

focused.description: Whether --focus switched a client (Open order step 8). A failed focus (no client, the client gone, a tmux error) is a warning: focused stays false and the open still succeeds.
